1.why: All six screens use a static, clean single-card layout with no animations, moving images, or pop-ups.

2.why: Bold headings, high-contrast teal primary buttons, and tinted info banners stand out well, though the actual reset code appears only in small monospace text inside the dark Logs panel.

3.why: Each screen presents one clearly labeled input and one primary action, so the needed element is found quickly, with slight difficulty only in locating codes within the Logs panel.

4.why: Instructions are displayed on each screen so little must be memorized, but the five-part password rule and the 10-minute code expiry still impose a noticeable memory load.

5.why: No password manager prompt, autofill option, or 'remember me' checkbox appears on any of the six screens.

6.why: No saved accounts, remembered credentials, or previously entered items are shown anywhere; only the repeated page layout offers familiarity.

7.why: Text is consistently short and plain (e.g., 'Codes expire after 10 minutes'), though terms like 'account identifier' and 'multi-factor code' are mildly technical.

8.why: No error messages appear in any of the six screenshots; only info and success banners are shown, so the claim cannot be confirmed.

9.why: Step 1 gives an explicit example of what to type ('use demo-account') and step 4 explains how to find the code, though no sample password is provided.

10.why: There is no choice among password, code, or face login; the flow is a single fixed code-based sequence with no face-login or alternative method offered.

11.why: Each screen offers at most one input and one or two buttons, so very few choices are presented at any one time.

12.why: A banner confirms the code was sent and the final screen summarizes all three completed outcomes, but intermediate confirmations (code verified, password saved) appear only in the technical Logs panel.

13.why: Every new step carries a short tip (code expiry, where to find the MFA code, safety reminders), though no dedicated help link or support channel exists.

14.why: A 'Request another code' button and a 'Return to recovery start' option provide clear retry paths, although no inline error-recovery flow is demonstrated.

15.why: The header, card layout, banner style, button design, Logs panel, and footer note remain identical across all six steps.
